questions.q: What is the key difference between a 'rejected' line and an 'error' line in the AutoInvoice Execution Report?
options: There is no difference; both terms mean the same thing
Rejected lines always become invoices eventually; error lines never do
A rejected line (missing setup) shows only a count with no reason, while an error line shows the actual error detail
Error lines only occur for tax issues
questions.explain: Rejected records (often due to missing setup like a customer account profile) show only as a count with no reason, while error records include the specific error detail in the report.

questions.q: Where do transaction lines land when AutoInvoice cannot import them?
options: RA_INTERFACE_ERRORS_ALL
GL_INTERFACE
AP_HOLDS_ALL
FA_MASS_ADDITIONS
questions.explain: Rejected or errored AutoInvoice transaction lines are transferred to RA_INTERFACE_ERRORS_ALL rather than becoming Receivables transactions.

questions.q: What was the shared root cause behind all 18 errored transactions at Meridian Steel Fabricators?
options: 18 unrelated customer setup issues
The invoices exceeded a credit limit
A closed accounting period
A new upstream product category was tagged with a tax rate code that had never been configured in Oracle Receivables
questions.explain: All 18 transactions came from the same new product category, which used a tax rate code that didn't exist in Receivables' tax setup, producing the same 'Invalid tax rate code' error for each.

questions.q: What happens to an invoice if just one line on it carries an invalid tax rate code?
options: Only that one line is rejected; the rest of the invoice imports normally
The entire invoice is rejected, not just the affected line
The invoice imports with a $0 tax amount
Oracle automatically assigns a default tax rate
questions.explain: An invalid tax rate code causes AutoInvoice to reject the entire invoice, since tax validation failure on any line blocks the whole transaction from importing.

questions.q: What was the correct resolution, rather than simply assigning any tax rate to make the error disappear?
options: Assign a random existing tax rate code to clear the error quickly
Disable tax validation in AutoInvoice
Add the correct, confirmed tax rate code to Receivables tax configuration after coordinating with whoever owns tax rates
Manually create the 18 invoices without tax
questions.explain: The fix required confirming the correct tax rate with the team that owns tax configuration, not inventing a rate just to clear the validation error.
